title: Verifier-Guided Repair of LLM-Generated Vendor CLI Configurations: A Controlled Fault-Injection Paired Study
abstract: We evaluate whether exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM-based repair workflow reduces residual unsafe or invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair. Following a preregistered controlled-challenge, paired design (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1) using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, we planned 40 confirmatory pairs and observed 39 complete pairs (one pair’s source generation was invalid and excluded per preregistration). Baseline (blind repair) passed the verifier+simulator acceptance predicate in 30/39 pairs (76.92%); guarded (verifier-guided) passed in 38/39 pairs (97.44%). Paired contingency counts: n11=29, n10=9 (guarded-only), n01=1 (baseline-only), n00=0. The paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.2051282051 (20.51 percentage points); two-sided exact paired test p = 0.021484375; 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.0769230769, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Execution used the declared model gpt-5-mini, recorded 118 hosted-model calls (budget 120), and archived all artifacts. We report preregistration adherence, exact execution accounting, statistical inference, and limitations (synthetic controlled faults, single model, simulator-backed success predicate) and provide an artifact bundle for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models are increasingly proposed to assist network operations by producing device configurations and remediation plans. Prior work shows that interposing deterministic verifiers in generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines can reduce verifier-detected failures in domains such as code and IaC [1]–[3], but systematic controlled evidence for vendor-CLI configuration repair and measured harmful-overrepair behaviour is limited. To provide preregistered, artifact-grounded evidence, we ask: Does a deterministic verifier-guided LLM repair pipeline reduce residual unsafe/invalid vendor-CLI configurations compared with blind repair when confronted with preregistered controlled faults? We contribute (1) a preregistered controlled-challenge paired experiment design and frozen task bank; (2) a completed confirmatory execution under hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared controlled-fault candidates; (3) a confirmatory paired analysis reporting a +20.51 percentage-point absolute increase in verifier+simulator pass rate for guarded versus baseline (p=0.021484375; 95% CI [0.0769230769,0.358974358974359]); and (4) an archived artifact bundle containing raw outputs, verifier traces, execution manifest, and analysis artifacts.
sections.related_work: Empirical GVR demonstrations in code and IaC indicate verifier-interposed repair can materially raise verifier pass rates and produce actionable diagnostics for repair [1]. Controlled verifier-first and verifier-guided evaluations on Infrastructure-as-Code report pass-rate improvements contingent on verifier design, retry budgets, and model choice [2]. Complementary analyses document a measurable verifier 'tax' (interaction length, cost) and identify verifier-exploitation risks where iterative optimization against a proxy verifier degrades the true target property [3]. Survey and field studies in NetOps report value for read/diagnostic assistance but weaker evidence for safe closed-loop configuration changes, motivating controlled-challenge evaluation on vendor CLIs to quantify post-repair residual invalidity and harmful edits [2]. (Cited works are listed by verified identifier in the artifact bundle; in-text numbered markers refer to that bundle.)
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand: We preregistered the study (vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1). Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Design and adapter semantics: confirmatory execution used adapter hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 with shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics: for each task index a single deterministically injected controlled-fault candidate was generated and shared unchanged across both conditions. Both conditions received exactly one repair opportunity; baseline is blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded is repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed to the model. Note: the archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Sampling semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per pair was performed and reused by both arms under the shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; all model-call runtime parameters and counts are recorded in the execution manifest. Task bank and controlled challenge: a deterministic fault injector produced 40 preregistered controlled-fault source candidates (controlled_fault_assignment_sha256 in the manifest). Confirmatory sample-size and stopping: task_count fixed at 40; preregistered stopping required abort if the adapter contract could not be satisfied. Execution: the declared model for confirmatory execution was gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version=gpt-5-mini). The acceptance predicate required both the deterministic vendor-CLI verifier and a simulator-based compliance agreement to avoid verifier↔simulator discordance. Analysis: primary test was an exact paired binary test (two-sided McNemar exact or equivalent); we report discordant-pair counts, absolute risk difference, and a 95% CI using paired-bootstrap percentile (resamples=10000, seed=1729). Missingness: per preregistration the 'complete_pair_primary' rule excludes a pair only if both condition executions fail for infrastructure reasons; one pair’s source generation was invalid/unscorable and excluded in accordance with this rule. All preregistered analysis options and sensitivity analyses were followed and are recorded in the archive.
sections.results: Execution accounting: planned confirmatory pairs = 40; completed episodes = 78 (39 complete pairs); failed episodes = 2; hosted-model calls used = 118 (≤ planned maximum 120); source-generation attempts = 40 (source_valid_count = 39; source_invalid_or_failed_count = 1). Primary outcomes (complete_pairs = 39): baseline success = 30/39 (0.7692307692307693); guarded success = 38/39 (0.9743589743589743). Paired contingency table: n11 (both pass) = 29; n10 (guarded-only pass) = 9; n01 (baseline-only pass) = 1; n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.20512820512820507 (20.51 percentage points). Exact two-sided paired test (McNemar exact): p = 0.021484375. 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI = [0.07692307692307693, 0.358974358974359] (bootstrap resamples = 10000, seed = 1729). Sensitivity and secondary analyses: preregistered exploratory per-fault-class summaries, harmful-change audits, and contamination checks (verifier↔simulator discordance flags) are archived and labelled exploratory; they are not used to support the primary confirmatory claim in this paper. No deviations from the preregistered primary analysis were made; the single unscorable pair exclusion is documented in the manifest.
sections.discussion: Under the preregistered controlled-challenge and shared-candidate pairing semantics, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to the model materially increased verifier+simulator-validated configuration success in our synthetic vendor-CLI task bank (approx. +20.5 pp). The paired shared-candidate design estimates the causal effect of exposing diagnostics on repair quality for the same injected fault candidate: both arms received the same preregistered controlled-fault candidate and identical repair budgets; only the diagnostic exposure differed. Interpretational boundaries and practical caveats: (1) external validity is limited — the confirmatory run used synthetic controlled faults, a single declared model (gpt-5-mini), and one deterministic verifier+simulator; results do not alone establish production generality across vendors, models, or operator policies; (2) intervention activation was ensured by deterministic fault injection (a design choice required to make the intervention testable); naturalistic activation rates in field workloads remain an open question; (3) operational feasibility (the verifier tax: interaction length, model-call cost, and latency) was instrumented and archived but requires larger-scale cost/latency tradeoff studies before deployment claims; (4) verifier-exploitation is a remaining risk in longer-horizon or multi-agent pipelines and requires mitigations (uncertainty quantification, calibrated abstention, multi-verifier schemes). All raw artifacts, verifier traces, provider call logs, and analysis files are archived to support independent verification and secondary analyses.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, controlled-fault paired experiment using the hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2 adapter and shared controlled-fault candidates, exposing deterministic verifier diagnostics to an LLM repair workflow produced a statistically detectable and substantial increase in verifier-and-simulator-validated configuration success (approx. +20.51 percentage points; p=0.021484375; 95% CI [0.0769230769,0.358974358974359]). The evidence demonstrates that, under controlled conditions and the archived execution contract, deterministic verifier diagnostics can materially affect repair outcomes. However, generalization to production NetOps requires cross-vendor, multi-model, and operational cost/latency evaluations; the archived artifact bundle supports such follow-up work.

disclosure_statement: Preregistration: vCLI_fault_injection_repair_2026_A_prereg_v1. Adapter: hosted_netops_validator_feedback_repair_v2. Declared model for confirmatory execution: gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version=gpt-5-mini). Exact initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: f781dd7978328198146d586cf33e0f4b783c8db126bd0f16fcd13699455ebb10) and cited here by immutable archive reference. Human role: a Research Director selected the topic family and pre-lock constraints; after the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature verification, preregistration, experiment execution, analysis, and manuscript generation; no manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the lock. Execution semantics: the archived model_configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. Pairing semantics: exactly one sampled initial generation per task pair was performed and reused by both arms under the shared_controlled_fault_candidate semantics; baseline denotes blind repair (no validator diagnostics exposed) and guarded denotes repair with deterministic validator diagnostics exposed. Artifact availability: the execution manifest, raw_results.jsonl, provider traces, verifier traces, analysis artifacts, and hashes are archived in the evidence bundle. The run followed the preregistered stopping rule and adapter contract; no silent adapter substitution occurred.
limitations: Synthetic controlled-fault task bank: tasks were deterministically injected and do not represent a broad naturalistic distribution of production NetOps incidents; external validity to live operator workloads is limited.
Single-model and single-adapter evaluation: confirmatory execution used only the declared model gpt-5-mini and one adapter family; results do not establish multi-model generality.
Simulator-backed primary success predicate: primary success required agreement of deterministic verifier and simulator; simulator fidelity and verifier coverage constrain construct validity.

Sample size and power: complete_pairs = 39 provides detectable effects of the observed magnitude but limits precision for subgroup and per-fault-class inference; exploratory subgroup analyses are not confirmatory.
Operational cost/latency unresolved for deployment: execution was instrumented and costs recorded, but large-scale operational feasibility (verifier tax tradeoffs) requires further study.

Verifier-exploitation and long-horizon agentic pathologies remain possible: this controlled setting mitigates some risks, but broader agentic workflows need additional defenses (uncertainty quantification, calibrated abstention, multi-verifier designs).
